newsitem.title: FRANCE: Communist leader Zyuganov urges Yeltsin to resign.
newsitem.headline: Communist leader Zyuganov urges Yeltsin to resign.

text.p: Russian Communist Party boss Gennady Zyuganov said on Monday President Boris Yeltsin should resign because of his heart condition.
"We have been asking Mr. Yeltsin for a long time to take the break we've been recommending and to let reforms follow their course," Zyuganov told Reuters on a visit to Strasbourg, eastern France.
Zyuganov, defeated by Yeltsin in a run-off for the Russian presidency in July, also said he believed the elections had been irregular because Yeltsin had misled voters about his health.
"It amounts to falsification. The elections were not fair," he said during a break in meetings at the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly which he was attending.
Asked if he wanted Yeltsin to resign, he said: "Yes".
Zyuganov said the Communist delegation to the 39-nation council would raise the question of Yeltsin's fitness to rule later on Monday at a session of the full parliamentary assembly.

In Moscow, the Communist speaker of Russia's State Duma lower house of parliament, Gennady Seleznyov, said Yeltsin should consider retiring if doctors rule he is unfit for heart surgery and ask him to cut down on his activity.

"I think that if the doctors give the president an exact diagnosis...how many hours he is able to work...and if they say this schedule is too restricted, so that it does not let the president work flat out, then in all probability he himself should ask to retire," Gennady Seleznyov told reporters.

Yeltsin, 65, said earlier this month he had agreed to undergo bypass surgery to improve blood supply to his heart. He said in a televised interview that the operation was likely to take place in late September.
But a surgeon tipped to lead the team preparing to operate on Yeltsin suggested at the weekend that the surgery might have to be postponed or even cancelled.

Russia's constitution says that the president should lay down his powers if he is found "persistently incapable" of carrying out his duties due to bad health. But it does not mention who can make such a decision.
